title: A same-day partial pool rerun replaces the earlier run's paid spend row, so pool verify (c) passes a correct record
goal: A same-day run of arm labels that overlap an earlier same-day run's paid: spend row replaces or splits that row (bench_pool.py near 1525), so pool verify (c) reads spend rows that equal the runs' costs; a record written before the fix (the 2026-10-09 record on work/ST-qiep6y7i, whose full spend row of 149.7418 USD still counts the 3.83 USD of the router runs the router-only rerun replaced) is repaired from its own rows by a benchmarks.py command, with no paid run, after which pool verify passes on it; tests.py -k bench_pool holds a test of the overlap that fails on today's code; found by the SP-2vhfsn4o review in a simulated rerun (spend row 2.5566 against runs 2.5834)

gates.question: When a same-day pool run's labels overlap an earlier same-day spend row, does the write path split the earlier row (drop the replaced labels from it, recomputed from the record's own rows, the new run's spend row beside it) or replace it (one row of the union of labels)?
options: split: the earlier row keeps its remaining labels, the new row stays beside it
replace: one combined row for the union of labels
gates.recommendation: split: the earlier row keeps its remaining labels, the new row stays beside it
gates.answer: split: the earlier row keeps its remaining labels, the new row stays beside it

notes: Added to SP-x7ger6vu by the operator on 2026-10-09: the router re-record of ST-qiep6y7i (run pool --arms router --reps 1, 3.62 USD) left pool verify failing (c), spend row 149.7418 against runs 149.5388; the operator chose the fix with an in-place repair of that record, no second paid run. The repair runs on work/ST-qiep6y7i after this item lands, so ST-qiep6y7i depends on it. tests.py -k bench_pool passes before the work: the overlap test the goal names is what makes it fail first.
